messages:
maria: FYI alert from CI and SLO dashboard — apac-a10 cluster p99 jump ~120ms after 4123 merged. Happening only on a10 pools, not h100/l4. @devin can you take a look?

devin: looking. seeing KV cache eviction rate spike correlated with throughput change. short/generative mixture looks worse. attaching profiler snippet.

maria: thanks. CI graph: https://ci.redwood.example/apac-a10/4123/p99 — you can see the step after deploy.

devin: paste of logs: ```kvcache_evictions/sec=134 -> 890 after merge, p99=420ms -> 550ms``` Also batch_size_avg jumped from 6 -> 14 for short requests.

asha: that batch_size change rings a bell — PR 4123 adjusted the batching heuristic to try to increase throughput for long sequences by favoring larger continuous batches. maybe it's overshooting for mixed workloads.

samir: repro locally on a10-emulator: run mix of 200x short (<=64) + 20x long (~1024) concurrent; see repeated kv cache thrash and context loads. KV cache hit rate drops from 92% -> 58%.

devin: minimal bisect plan: revert batching heuristic in runtime (PR 4123) on canary apac-a10, re-run CI perf job. if that restores kv hit rate and p99, we confirm.

maria: is the problem strictly the heuristic or an interaction with the new kernel selector fallback? 4123 also touched kernel-selection thresholds.

devin: good point. I instrumented kernel-picker: on a10 the selector is now preferring the quantized fallback path for certain seq distributions. fallback path allocates more KV memory per context, combined with larger batches causes eviction. So it's both: batch size up + fallback path = double whammy.

ops-bot: deploy canary start: rollout/apac-a10/canary -> sha:abcd1234 (revert-4123)

asha: quick config we can try without full revert: force kernel_selector.threshold_seq_len=256 and batching.max_continuous_batch=8 for apac-a10. That should reduce fallback and cap batch expansion.

maria: please apply as a scoped config then run perf smoke. If it fixes, we can ship a targeted rollout instead of full revert.

devin: applied scoped config to canary and kicked CI. smoke results: p99 back to baseline, kvcache evictions dropped to 120/sec, kv hit rate 89%. CI perf job passing so far.

ci-bot: perf-check: apac-a10-canary — p50: 12ms (-), p95: 78ms (-), p99: 128ms (baseline 125ms) -> PASS (no regression).

samir: great. we should follow up with a root cause PR: split the batching heuristic into workload-aware mode and add a safety cap for continuous batch growth. also update kernel selector to consider kv footprint cost when choosing fallback.

asha: agree. I'll draft PR with tests and a microbenchmark to catch regressions (short/long mixed workload).

maria: thanks team. action items: 1) ash a draft PR to revert heuristics or introduce guard (asha), 2) update kernel selector cost model (devin), 3) add canary perf check to release pipeline (samir), 4) monitor apac-a10 for 24h (maria).

devin: one more note: this only showed up on a10 due to its smaller per-chip KV allocation vs h100 and different memory allocator behavior. calling out hardware-specific footguns in release notes.

maria: noted. logging followup in incident tracker: https://incidents.redwood.example/INC-2026. closing thread after 24h stable. :thumbsup:
